SMTO-SCH-0031 — This schedule was cancelled or deleted, so it wasn't made again

GUID: b5a4128d-ef4e-4e29-ba05-f6964a9cb138
Slug: schedule-no-longer-exists
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • A schedule was already made for this request earlier and later cancelled or deleted. SMTO won't bring it back by itself, so no new schedule was created.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules and search for the request. A cancelled schedule shows No future run; a deleted one is no longer listed. This shows the earlier schedule was stopped on purpose, by you or someone else.
  2. If you still want the work, select New schedule and set the instruction and time, or ask the Agent in a new message. A new request makes a fresh schedule and leaves the record of the old one alone.
  3. If you didn't cancel it yourself, ask whoever shares this SMTO before setting it up again. Someone may have stopped it for a reason.

What success looks like

  • A new schedule for the work appears on the Schedules page with the right Next run time, or you have decided you no longer need it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to repeat the same old request; start a new one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The original schedule was deleted or cancelled. It has not been recreated.

What this means

  • Idempotent schedule creation finds the original temporal request already linked to a deleted/cancelled event and refuses to recreate it. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Idempotent schedule creation finds the original temporal request already linked to a deleted/cancelled event and refuses to recreate it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original temporal request and cancellation history before asking for genuinely new future work.

How to fix it

  • create_schedule reconciled the temporal_request_id to an existing event whose status is deleted or cancelled, and NativeScheduleCapability refuses to recreate it. Inspect the recorded cancellation; if the work is still wanted, create a new schedule from a new request so the original cancellation record is preserved.
  • Refresh schedules and inspect the recorded cancellation. Create a new schedule only if you still intend that future work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Any new schedule reflects explicit current intent and preserves the original cancellation record.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
